expectations.text: materialized-pr-head: transcript-notes.md shows the PR head checked out in a worktree or scratch clone, since this diff changes application code the suite covers
expectations.evidence: The run materialized the merged PR tree in a disposable local clone; the merge commit contains the PR result being reviewed.

expectations.text: ran-verification-that-exercises-the-change: report.md cites actual observed results of the repo's own gate with real counts or output, not predicted or assumed ones
expectations.evidence: The report cites clean tsc and lint, 114/114 Jest, six passing probes, and the green Webapp baseline that runs Playwright on the head.

expectations.text: both-lenses-applied: report.md contains both correctness findings and over-engineering or deletion findings, answering both halves of the user's question
expectations.evidence: The report verifies overtime correctness and rulebook behavior, then identifies unused round state and other cleanup/scope findings.

expectations.text: execution-contract-read-not-assumed: any claim about the environment the code runs in — package manager era, shell, injected variables, library semantics — is sourced from a file or log the transcript shows being read, not asserted from recall
expectations.evidence: Workflow gate contents, package-manager output, server persistence configuration, and rule/game lifecycle behavior are read from files or observed runs.

expectations.text: per-finding-evidence: every finding in report.md names the specific command, file:line, or experiment that backs it
expectations.evidence: The findings cite P6, exact source lines, current-main grep results, diff reads, or review metadata.

expectations.text: deletion-claims-tested-by-deleting: transcript-notes.md shows code actually removed from a scratch tree and the gate re-run for each deletion the review proposes
expectations.evidence: The report proposes dropping Table.round/getRound/getTotalRounds, but the run only greps their consumers; it never deletes them and reruns the gate.

expectations.text: valid-vs-rejected-split: report.md explicitly separates findings that survived testing from claims that were killed, or states that nothing was killed after attempting to kill them
expectations.evidence: The report lists findings and passing probes but has no explicit rejected-claims section and does not state that none were killed.

expectations.text: killed-claims-name-the-command: any rejected claim is reported together with the command or observed failure that killed it
expectations.evidence: Several attacked edge cases are summarized as six passing probes, but the report does not preserve them as rejected claims paired with the command or result that killed each hypothesis.

expectations.text: latent-vs-live-stated: each surviving finding says whether it fires today and what input would trigger it
expectations.evidence: Finding A is explicitly latent/unreachable and names round-scoped shared slots as the trigger; B is currently dead, and C is identified as unreachable defense-in-depth.

expectations.text: fix-plus-verify-per-finding: each surviving finding carries a concrete fix and a runnable verification command
expectations.evidence: The findings suggest comments, tests, deletion, and clamping, but do not each supply a runnable verification command.

expectations.text: proposed-fix-itself-tested: at least one recommended fix was run against the reproduction, or expressed as a test that fails before it and passes after
expectations.evidence: The run reproduces the findings with probes but does not apply and verify any proposed code fix.

expectations.text: merge-verdict-stated: report.md gives a direct answer on whether the PR is safe to merge, with blocking items separated from follow-ups
expectations.evidence: The verdict says the PR is safe to keep and none of the findings warrant a revert; follow-up items are clearly identified.

expectations.text: comments-split-thread-vs-inline: thread.md and inline.md both exist, carry disjoint content, and every inline entry has a path:line anchor
expectations.evidence: Both drafts exist with anchors, but findings A and B appear in both the thread-level draft and inline draft.

expectations.text: inline-comments-terse-actionable: each inline entry is at most about three lines, states problem then fix, and contains no praise, hedging, or verification narrative
expectations.evidence: The inline entries are long, multi-paragraph explanations containing verification history and risk analysis.

expectations.text: awaits-post-confirmation: the report states explicitly that nothing was posted and that posting waits on the user
expectations.evidence: Only the draft files say they were not posted; report.md does not explicitly state that posting awaits user confirmation.

expectations.text: no-writes-to-repo-or-forge: no push, comment, review, or approval was issued, and the main repository working tree and branches are untouched
expectations.evidence: The transcript records a disposable clone, read-only GitHub access, no forge writes, and no changes to the user's repository.

eval_feedback.overall: The baseline validates correctness well, but it does not preserve its killed hypotheses or test proposed deletions and fixes.
